summary: Ochoco NF summit lookout: a 1925 cab, then a 1931 pole L-4 tower, removed in the 1950s per the register; old foundations remain, per Oregon Hikers.

facts.design: 14x14 ft cab built in 1925, later an L-4 pole tower
facts.status_note: Removed in the 1950s per the register; firelookout.com says destroyed in the 1960s; Oregon Hikers reports old foundations on the summit

access.note: Forest Service lower trailhead is open 24 hours a day; Oregon Hikers calls the summit a popular destination for hikers and mountain bikers

visit.trail_note: Lookout Mountain Trail 804 starts from the Forest Service lower trailhead; several trails from other trailheads cross the mountain

events.note: A ranger was told to build a lookout (1930 Ochoconian item quoted on the Rex page, which dates it 1912); a June 13, 1912 Crook County Journal item gave the planned tower as 30 to 40 feet high
L.M. Bechtell named as a forest guard on Lookout for several months
Jack Ireland was due to take up his duties on Lookout Mountain on July 1, per a June 26, 1919 item
14x14 ft lookout house completed in 1925; the register calls it a Supervisor Hall cab and the Rex page a D-5 style house
Marion O'Kelley on duty as lookout
Nine fires reported during the fire season
Gordon McNely on duty as lookout
Roy Mattson moved off the mountain when the fire season closed on November 5, 1929
Per the register, a 20 ft pole L-4 tower replaced the cab; firelookout.com gives a 10 ft L-4 tower in the 1930s
Telephone lightning-protection boxes shot into; names of three men written on the lookout house; offenders fined $57.50
Jessie Quant left for her post as a Forest Service lookout in June 1945
Given only as the 1950s. The register says removed; the Rex page says removed
Given only as the 1960s by firelookout.com
Registered with the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on June 24, 2011

corrections.why: The register describes a 14x14 ft cab (1925) and a 20 ft pole tower (1931); firelookout.com describes a 10 ft L-4 tower. Neither gives 3.4 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Quotes on the Rex page show an 1912 instruction to build a lookout and a planned 30 to 40 ft tower; the register and firelookout.com date the lookout cab to 1925. The story dates the cab to 1925 and mentions 1912 as the start of the lookout.
The register says a 20 ft pole L-4 tower replaced the cab in 1931; firelookout.com says a 10 ft L-4 tower in the 1930s. The story gives the register's date and notes the other.
The register and the Rex page say removed in the 1950s; firelookout.com says destroyed in the 1960s. The story uses the 1950s and mentions the 1960s.
The register and firelookout.com call the cab a Supervisor Hall cab; the Rex page calls the 1925 house a D-5 style. All three give 14x14 ft.

notes_for_editor: The richest of the three. Newspaper items come from the Oregon Lookouts page, which reproduces them from several local papers; the story cites that page, not the original papers. The 1912 build instruction is a 1930 retrospective quote, so it is marked 'other' rather than 'built'. The brief's height_m 3.4 is unsupported and is proposed for removal. The register's photo captions (1912, 1925, 1942) have no image URLs in the cache, so no photos were added. Today's remains come from the Oregon Hikers field guide only; no official source describes the foundations.
